newsitem.title: USA: CoreStates Q2 chargeoffs up versus Q1.
newsitem.headline: CoreStates Q2 chargeoffs up versus Q1.

text.p: CoreStates Financial Corp said Wednesday net charge-offs were $62.7 million in the second quarter compared with $49.3 million in the first quarter and $70.7 million in the 1996 second quarter.

The 1996 second quarter charge-offs included $34 million related to the April 1996 acquisition of Meridian Bancorp and $5.8 million related to a policy change to charge off delinquent credit card accounts at 150 days instead of 180. Excluding the merger-related and policy change charge-offs a year ago, the year-over-year increase in net charge-offs was 103 percent.

"We are continuing to see a high level of retail charge-offs, especially credit card charge-offs, and these are the bulk of what we're reporting," chairman Terrence Larsen said in a statement. "This quarter, however, slightly more than half of the increase in charge-offs compared to the first quarter was on the wholesale side."

CoreStates said total non-performing assets at June 30 were $282 million, up from $259 million in the first quarter and $254 million a year ago. The $282 million represented 0.6 percent of total assets and 0.8 percent of total loans plus real estate foreclosed as of June 30.
Larsen said the increase in non-performing assets was attributable to the addition of three wholesale accounts totaling $51 million to non-performing assets.

Larsen said CoreStates felt it "appropriate to make a fairly aggressive increase in the loan loss provision. At this point in the business cycle, it's only prudent to anticipate that there is in fact still a business cycle and that we should be prepared to deal with a normal, cyclical deterioration in credit quality."

CoreStates said the second-quarter 1997 loan loss provision was $50 million, compared with $43 million in the first quarter and $40 million on an operating basis, excluding a special provision in connection with the acquisition, in the second quarter a year ago.
The reserve for possible loan losses at June 30 was $691 million, or 2.0 percent of total loans and 262 percent of total non-performing loans.
Overall, CoreStates reported operating earnings of $0.97 per share in the second quarter versus $0.88 a year ago, representing an increase of 10.2 percent.

Net income on an operating basis was $199.7 million in the 1997 second quarter versus $193.4 million a year ago, an increase of 3.3 percent. The per-share results were affected by share repurchases with average shares outstanding falling to 205.0 million in the quarter from 219.5 million a year ago.

The company's authorization to repurchase 10 percent or 22 million shares by the end of 1997 was about 98 percent complete after a privately-negotiated repurchase of six million shares in mid-June. The board voted Tuesday to extend the program and authorized repurchase of up to three percent of outstanding shares, or six million shares, by year-end.
